extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, agents and examiners dealing with PCT national-phase filings and prosecution in India
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on fees, withdrawal, amendments, international preliminary examination, entry into the Indian national phase, publication, request for examination, formal and substantive examination procedure, novelty search strategy, and post-filing actions under the Indian Patents Act and PCT rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Fee deadline and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Fee is for the benefit of the International Bureau. It is intended to cover the cost of the work the International Bureau must perform under the PCT. The amounts are fixed in the Schedule of Fees, which forms part of the regulations. The international fee is due within one month from the date of receipt of the International Application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay within one month of receipt of the international application; amounts are fixed in the Schedule of Fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search Fee deadline and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The Search Fee is for the benefit of the International Searching Authority. It is intended to compensate that Authority for the work it must perform in connection with the establishment of the international search report. It is due within one month from the date of receipt of the International Application. The amount is fixed by the International Searching Authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay within one month; amount varies by ISA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal to prevent publication — timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the intent of the withdrawal is to prevent publication, the notice of withdrawal must reach the International Bureau before technical preparations for international publication have been completed (that is, not later than 15 days before the date of publication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To stop publication, withdraw early enough so IB receives notice ≥15 days before scheduled publication; otherwise publication proceeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional withdrawal effective only if publication prevented
rubrics_metrics.description: A withdrawal of an International Application can be made with the condition that the withdrawal be effective only if the international publication can still be prevented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may file conditional withdrawals tied to whether publication can be stopped; this preserves options if timing uncertain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article 19: One-time amendment of claims after international search
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims can be adjusted to the results of the international search report by amending them once (under Article 19) with effect in all designated States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Article 19 amendment to harmonize claims across designated states; saves multiple national amendments and costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments during national phase and Chapter II
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual amendments before each designated Office are also permitted in the national phase (under Article 28 or 41) and all parts of the application can be amended (under Article 34(2)) during the international preliminary examination procedure under Chapter II.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may still amend in national phase; Chapter II permits broader amendments during international preliminary examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Preliminary Examination (optional) — purpose and benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: International Preliminary Examination (optional) provides, in addition to the international search report, an international preliminary examination report containing an opinion on the usual criteria of patentability before expenses are incurred for the national phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benefits include: opinion on patentability and probability of obtaining a patent; helps adapt application to search results; allows amending all parts of the application (description, claims, drawings) with effect for elected Offices; may reduce costs and make application more ready for acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPEA fees structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary examination fees differ by IPEA and include handling fees; amounts (example table) are set and vary by authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the applicable IPEA’s fee schedule and handling fee; amounts were listed (e.g., AT EUR 159, AU AUD 550/1000, CN CNY 1,500, EP EUR 1,530, SE SEK 5,000, US USD 600) and handling fees in CHF.

rubrics_metrics.name: National phase entry: acts required and consequences of non-entry
rubrics_metrics.description: In the national phase before processing and examination in the designated or elected Offices, the applicant must perform certain acts thereby effecting 'entry into the national phase.' If the applicant does not enter the national phase, namely, if he does not perform these acts within the prescribed time limit, the International Application loses its effect in the designated or elected States concerned with the same consequences as the withdrawal of any national application in that State (Article 24).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform required acts within prescribed time limits (e.g., pay national fees, file translations) to preserve rights; failure equals loss of application in that State.

rubrics_metrics.name: National phase entry acts: fees and translations
rubrics_metrics.description: For entry into the national phase before a designated or elected Office it is necessary that the national fee be paid to it and, where the International Application has not been filed or published in the official language, or one of the official languages of that Office, a translation into an official language be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File translations when required and pay national fees; note some Offices have longer time limits than 31 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: National fees and possible reductions/refunds
rubrics_metrics.description: The national fees to be paid are usually same as the fees required for the filing of a national or regional application. Some Offices levy lower fees, or refund certain fees, on account of the existence of the international search report or where an international preliminary examination report has been established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some Offices offer reductions (examples: EPO search/exam reductions, German/Hungarian filing/exam fee waivers/reductions, Japan large reductions when JPO ISA, UK refunds). Check country-specific rules to estimate costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of original drawings for national phase economies
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the original drawings are of a good quality, the applicant is not required to file additional formal drawings with the Designated or Elected Offices, permitting substantial economies in some cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure drawings filed with the Receiving Office fully comply with PCT format requirements to avoid refiling drawings in national phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority document certified copy handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the priority of an earlier application is claimed and a certified copy of that application has been provided, it is not necessary to submit a certified copy of the priority document to each designated or elected Office. The International Bureau sends any required copies of the priority document to the Offices concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide certified priority document to IB to avoid repeated submissions to each designated Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal remedies for procedural loss (review, reinstatement, further processing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where, as a result of a mistake which was not timely corrected, an International Application is considered withdrawn, the applicant may request review of that decision by each of the designated Offices. In addition the applicant has the opportunity to submit a request for excuse of failure to comply with a time limit; where law provides for reinstatement this can be requested; further processing may be possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remedies depend on applicable national law or regional convention; applicants should seek review, excuse requests, reinstatement or further processing where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic requirements to enter national phase in India (documents & fees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the basic requirements to start the national phase in India, the applicant is required to file the following with the DO/IN or EO/IN within the prescribed time limit: (i) An application on a plain paper (Form 1 may be used but optional); (ii) National fee in INR: INR 1,000 for individual(s) INR 4,000 for legal entity (with multiple fees for multiple priorities); (iii) Where the international application has not been filed or published in Hindi or English, a translation of the application (description, claims, abstract) should be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with form, translation and fee requirements within the national-phase time limit; multiple priority claims incur multiple fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT Rule 51bis special requirements (what cannot be demanded early)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under PCT Rules 51bis, no designated Office is to require before the expiration of the applicable time limit for entering the national phase the performance of acts other than those referred to in Article 22 (payment of national fee, furnishing translation and, in exceptional cases, furnishing copy and name/address of inventor). All other requirements of national law are 'special requirements' and may be complied with once national processing has started.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated Offices must not demand special national formalities before national-phase entry; applicants may defer these until national processing begins.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of special national requirements for India (Form and documentary needs)
rubrics_metrics.description: As per DO/IN or EO/IN the special requirements of the Office include: a) Name, nationality and address of the inventor if not in the 'Request'; b) Instrument of assignment or transfer where applicant is not the inventor; c) Document evidencing change of name of the applicant if occurred after filing date (Form PCT/IB/306) and Form 6 and/or Form 13 as required; d) Declaration of inventorship; e) Statement regarding filing of corresponding applications in other countries; f) Power of attorney if an agent is appointed; g) Address for service in India; h) Verification of translation; i) Copy of international application or its translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare these documents for submission if requested after national-phase entry; representation by an agent is not mandatory but power of attorney may be required if agent appointed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication numbering and PCT national-phase timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Immediately on receiving the application patent office accords an application number to it such that the applications filed in a year constitute a series identified by the year of such filing. PCT National Phase applications constitute a different series (Rule 11). In case of PCT National phase applications processing of the application starts only after the expiry of 31 months from its priority (R.20(2) and R.20(4)) but may be taken up for examination before the said period on express request of the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect separate numbering for national-phase PCT apps; default processing waits until 31 months unless applicant requests earlier examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screening before publication (categorization and defense relevance)
rubrics_metrics.description: All the applications will be screened to categorize the invention to the respective field of technology and to find whether the invention is relevant for defense purposes etc. so that the necessary procedures can be initiated in respect of those files tested positive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications may be held for additional procedures if flagged for defense/security relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early publication request (Form 9) and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant makes a request in Form 9 (before the expiry of 18 months) with the prescribed fee (Rs. 2,500 for individual natural person(s) and Rs. 10,000 for legal entity other than natural person(s)), the application will be published as soon as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File Form 9 and pay fee to obtain publication before the regular 18-month date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances when application will not be published
rubrics_metrics.description: The application will not be published if secrecy direction is given under Section 35 or has been abandoned under section 9 or has been withdrawn 3 months prior to the expiry of 18 months. In case a secrecy direction has been given it will be published after the expiry of the 18-month period or when the secrecy direction is lifted, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secrecy directions, abandonment and timely withdrawals prevent publication; secrecy direction suspends publication until revoked or 18 months pass.

rubrics_metrics.name: Particulars included in publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The particulars of publication are: Date of the Application; Number of the Application; Name of the Applicant; Address of the Applicant; Abstract of the Invention. Publication will be identified by the letter 'A' along with the number of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect those bibliographic data in the published patent application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of publication (public availability and provisional rights)
rubrics_metrics.description: The depository institution will make any biological material mentioned in the specification available to the public. The Patent office will make the specification and drawing available to the public on payment of prescribed fee. The applicant shall have like privileges and rights as if a patent for the invention had been granted from the date of publication of the application until the date of grant, but he shall not be entitled to institute any proceedings for infringement until the patent has been granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication triggers public access to materials and provisional rights accrue from publication date (subject to limitations); check fees for public access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferred Examination system: request timing and advantages
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications will be taken up for examination only on request in Form 18 made after the publication of application (within 36 months from the date of priority or from the date of filing whichever is earlier) by the applicant or a person interested with the prescribed fee. This system of examination is called Deferred Examination system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advantages include obtaining priority date without paying exam fee, recognition of inventor, the ability to delay examination up to 36 months to obtain funding, and third parties being able to request examination and later license. File Form 18 and pay fees within 36 months to trigger examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for examination deadlines and consequence of non-request
rubrics_metrics.description: Request for examination can be made only after publication and within 36 months from the date of filing or date of priority of the application whichever is earlier. For applications filed before 1 Jan 2005 the request should be made within 48 months. If no request for examination is made within the prescribed period the application will be treated as withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure examination request is filed within the applicable deadline (36/48 months) or the application is treated as withdrawn; special rules apply where secrecy direction was issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of examination and First Examination Report (FER)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications will be taken up for examination according to the order in which the request is made. The Controller refers the application to an Examiner whether the application, specification and other documents related thereto are in compliance of the Act and Rules. The examiner has to make a report to the Controller within a period of 1 month from the date of such reference. This Report is called First Examination Report (FER).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examination queue is request-order based; expect an FER within the statutory timeframe after referral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal examination file order and handling (office practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers should be kept in specific ordered sets: Set 1 (Office Notes and correspondence), Set 2 (Main Documents including forms and specifications), Set 3 (Supporting Documents like assignments and certificates), Set 4 (Additional copies). Initials and signatures should be placed as required; date stamps on each document; amended documents should supersede originals and be endorsed 'superseded'; supporting documents should be sent to the applicant along with objections if no attestation; cross-reference co-pending applications; files transmitted to examiners immediately after formal examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the prescribed office filing order and stamping/signature practices to ensure correct processing and traceability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal examination checks (required data and conformity)
rubrics_metrics.description: It should be ensured that all the documents are in conformity with the act and rules; nationality and address of applicant and inventor are stated; checking should be made to confirm that all the necessary details under S.8 are furnished; checking whether the agent is registered and named in PA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify completeness of administrative data and compliance with S.8 and agent registration to avoid procedural objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive/technical examination core criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical and legal matters mainly include exploration of: (1) Whether the subject matter is an invention within the meaning of Section 2(l)(j), based on the criteria of Novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability; (2) Whether the invention is one which is not patentable under Sections 3 & 4; (3) Whether the specification complies with the requirements of Section 10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive exam tests patentability (novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability), statutory exclusions, and formal sufficiency of the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of substantive examination steps
rubrics_metrics.description: The examination of the application proceeds in the following order: 1) Understanding of the invention; 2) Assessment of Patentability of the subject matter; 3) Assessment of sufficiency of disclosure; 4) Check for unity of invention; 5) Appraisal of Industrial applicability; 6) Classification of the invention; 7) Determination of priority of each claim; 8) Novelty search; 9) Determination of the inventive step; 10) Judgment of the validity of claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow this sequential procedure when examining or preparing an application to anticipate examiner scrutiny and objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles for novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: The examination of industrial applicability is based on the technical documentation in the patent application dossier, while the examination of novelty and inventive step requires documentary search; before examination of novelty and inventive step it is necessary to check whether the invention is fully defined, feasible and applicable; novelty is determined before inventive step because the creative contribution can be assessed only by knowing the novel elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure full definition and feasibility in the disclosure before evaluating novelty/inventiveness; perform searches for prior art to support novelty and inventive-step conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy for novelty search — classification first
rubrics_metrics.description: Every search for novelty should start only after the classification of the invention. While classifying, one main classification and two or three closely related classifications shall be determined by the Examiner. The search shall be concentrated on the relevant fields of the classification and within such field search can be intensified by giving the 'key words' from the description. MIMOSA databases are useful for determining classification by keyword search. Search should also be conducted in publications other than patent documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with IPC/other classification, select main+related classes, use keywords from the description, search patent and non-patent literature, and choose databases based on the nature of the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indian standard: Relative novelty (not absolute) and documents to consider
rubrics_metrics.description: Indian Patents Act requires Relative Novelty (not Absolute Novelty). The examiner should search whether the invention claimed has been anticipated by: a) Indian patent specifications published before the date of filing but on or after 01.01.1912 (S.13(1)(a)); b) Indian patent specifications filed before the date of filing or claiming earlier priority but published on or after the filing date (S.13(1)(b)); c) Any publication in India or elsewhere effected before the filing date (S.13(2)); d) Indian patent specifications published before the date of filing but on or after the priority date of the application (S.13(1)(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search scope is defined by Indian statute — consider relevant Indian and foreign publications as specified; be mindful of priority dates and publication dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation document types and significance (X and Y)
rubrics_metrics.description: According to international standards the search should result in documents which form citation types: A, E, L, O, P, T, X, Y & (descriptions in annexure). The citations of the type X and Y are very important as they explicitly indicate lack of novelty and obviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay special attention to X and Y citations in search results since they indicate strong prior-art objections (novelty/obviousness).

rubrics_metrics.name: What are not anticipations (S.29–S.33) — exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Exceptions include: (a) Previous publication before 1912 not deemed anticipation; (b) Previous publication before priority date may not anticipate if matter was obtained from inventor without their knowledge and application made immediately after discovery (subject to limits); (c) Communication to Government for investigation does not anticipate; (d) Public display/exhibition: if application made by inventor within 12 months after exhibition, disclosure at exhibition not an anticipation; (e) Public working for reasonable trial within one year before priority date by inventor or with consent not an anticipation; (f) Use/publication after provisional specification filing does not anticipate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutory exceptions may preserve patentability despite earlier disclosures in limited circumstances; evidence and timing are critical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions the Controller may take in cases of anticipation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the invention is anticipated by prior publication as per S.13 the Controller may refuse the complete specification unless the applicant shows that the priority date of his claim is not later than that of the cited document or amends the complete specification to the Controller's satisfaction. If anticipated by prior claiming (S.13(1)(b)) the Controller may direct that a reference to that other specification be inserted in the applicant's specification unless the applicant shows an earlier priority date or amends. The Controller may also direct insertion of a reference to another patent which could be infringed and may delete such reference later on request when conditions change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When anticipation is found, remedies include refusal, mandated insertion of references, or allowing amendments; applicants should consider priority evidence or claim amendments to overcome objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-conclusiveness of Section 13 investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: The investigation made under Section 13 is not deemed to be conclusive on the question of anticipation and central government or its officers incur no liability (S.13(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner's search or Controller's finding under S.13 is not final proof; further proceedings (e.g., litigation, opposition) can revisit anticipation findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: FER issuance, applicant response period and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: The gist of objections in the First Examination Report (FER) will be communicated to the applicant. The applicant will be allowed to carry out necessary amendments in compliance with Rule 14. The time for meeting the objections and putting the application in order is 6 months from the date of issue of FER. This time may be extended only once for a further period not exceeding 3 months by the Controller in circumstances beyond the control of the applicant when a request is made in FORM 4 with specified fee; otherwise the application will be deemed abandoned. For FERs issued before the Patents (Amendment) Act 2005 the time was twelve months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to FER within 6 months (or extended 3 months if Controller allows upon form & fee) or risk abandonment; prepare amendments and requests for hearings as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amended specification examined same as original
rubrics_metrics.description: The amended specification should be examined in the same way as the original specification (S.13(3)). There can be many correspondences between the examiner and the applicant after the issue of FER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect amended specs to be scrutinized to the same standards as originals; iterative correspondence is normal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-dating an application (S.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: The application for patent may be post-dated to a date not later than six months from the date of the application on request of the applicant (made at any time before the grant of patent) along with the prescribed fee. This does not apply if the application is deemed abandoned per S.9(1). If the specification is amended under section 15 and the Controller feels that post-dating is required he may direct that the application or specification be deemed to have been made on the date on which the requirements are complied with or re-filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use post-dating cautiously; filing a request with fee can change the effective application date up to six months under S.17, subject to Controller discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change/substitution of applicant (S.20) — procedure and proof
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim for substituting an applicant/applicants has to be made in Form 6 with the prescribed fee along with the original assignment/agreement or an official/notarized copy thereof. The Controller may call for other proof of title or written consent of the assignor/s if required. By virtue of a written assignment or agreement from the applicant or by operation of law the claimant(s) may claim the patent or specific interest; the Controller, if satisfied, may direct that the application proceed in the name of the claimant(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File Form 6 and attach assignment documents and fee; be prepared to supply further evidence of title if Controller requests.
